analysis:
Examined the supplied base tail (lines 3081-3442) and head start (lines 1-485) of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift. Visible head content is mostly the unchanged pure-Foundation onboarding model types. Of the changed ranges, only the patch excerpt is visible for head 1518-1525, and the new closures there are default no-ops. Base 3081-3442 covers start, wait, provision and busy helpers; the corresponding head regions (about 3060-3445) are not in the supplied head unit.

Changed security behavior: the PR adds `stopsAsked` and `serveUnlessStopped` hooks, and `provision` gains a `stopsBefore:` parameter. They guard against a start undoing a user-requested stop (stop-versus-start race). This is local lifecycle/availability logic (A-018, TB-012 area) and is not a trust boundary against a remote adversary. The default closures are inert (`{ nil }` and `nil`). The stop-count check is claimed to run on the leading Mac under the start lock, but that implementation is outside the supplied evidence.

Other examined behavior: `ClusterServingScope` bind validation (`isValidBind` uses inet_pton or "localhost"). Invalid saved binds fall back to loopback, not wider. The default for local-only is 0.0.0.0 by owner decision, an existing behavior. The private image qualification gating (`privateQualificationRefusal`) is unchanged and restricts to local scope and leader role. No changes touch the coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), prompt encryption, key custody, or the cache.

Remaining questions for integration: (1) the `.live` implementation of `serveUnlessStopped` and `stopsAsked` (the ClusterSetupRecord lock and counter, and whether a stale or unreadable count fails open to serving after a stop, i.e. whether nil means serve unconditionally); (2) the head edits at about 2982-3013 and 3518-3539, which were not supplied. No concrete regression is identifiable from the supplied lines.
